fields.says: A run-row field that is always present with a default is one entry in `RUN_FIELDS` (`lib/dispatch-fields.js`). A sparse field stays a conditional spread in `addItem` and `_archiveItem`, so other rows keep their key sets byte-identical. Six fields were once dropped on one hop of four.
Every exit from the queue except a take archives through `_archiveItem` (`lib/dispatch-store.js`); a new exit must archive through it too.

The wake path is `_planWake` (decide) then `_deliverWake` (deliver) in `lib/dispatch-store.js`, shared by `addFeedback` and the held-wake release (LIN-4373). Its guards (LIN-1059, 1165, 1357, 2297, 4080, 4166) run in an order that matters: change the pair whole, keep the wake suites passing, and update the two census pins (`lin-3134-declared-mint-census`, `lin-4080-addItem-census`) if the write moves.
"This run's PR" is the session's own report: `prUrlOfFeedback` (`lib/dispatch-wake.js`) takes a PR on a report line before the `[done]` `url`, which older runners filled by mention count (LIN-4375).

Two `[done]` posts can reach a decide-then-enqueue at once, so "no row yet" is no guard: claim first, compare-and-set on the row (`claimHeldWake`). LIN-4373 relied on the read and queued two leftover rows (LIN-4375).
A claim whose holder skips is released on every path out (`releaseHeldWakeClaim`). A stamp left by a skip held the re-report forever (LIN-4375 review).

Any session can park `[pending]` on CI and finish on a ci-wake `custom` row (`lib/ci-wake-sweep.js`). A rule keyed on the producing kind misses that ending: read the lineage (`heldWakeHolderOf`, `resolveFollowUpRoot`). LIN-4373 covered eligibility, not the held wake's terminals.

Row-only kinds stay out of `DISPATCH_KINDS` (`lib/prompt-templates.js`) and sit in `ROW_ONLY_KINDS` (`lib/dispatch-fields.js`); kind-keyed maps are tested against both. A new bucket can pull a kind into the round-trip walk, which `OFF_SPINE_KINDS` stops (LIN-4376).

The store knows no leftovers (LIN-4383). It holds a parent wake by `heldWakeFor` (LIN-4373), released by the holder's terminal or `_archiveItem` under the build's guard key, so it wakes once. Leftover wording lives in `lib/dispatch-leftover-hook.js`; a new held-wake feature brings a hook (`lin-4377-store-knows-no-leftover` counts the word).
Price a pulled extra like any piece: a cost read that rode along with LIN-4201 landed alone as LIN-4226.

A task timeline lane is running from the page's open session ids (`isOpenState`), never the cost row; a lineage's own `incomplete`, not the shared `lineagesTruncated`, decides "not complete" (LIN-4405, `lib/task-timeline.js`).

A test that dispatches a close-out passes a `closeOut` seam (`resolveProvider`): the readiness guard reads comments for every close-out since LIN-4438, and without the seam it reaches the real provider and fails open, a pass the hermetic watcher catches only in CI.

Close-out readiness has five lanes: the route (`codeRouteOf`), the stop-at state, the task page's box (`buildRunEvidence`) and both guard lanes (`closeOutNotReady`). A readiness rule goes in `closeOutWaitsOn` (`lib/run-closeout-state.js`) and gets a row in the shared-trail table (`lin-4438-blind-read-gate`); gating one lane let the page offer a press the guard refused (LIN-4438).

A reader that classifies by kind routes `custom` before `bucketOf`: `BUCKET_OF_KIND` maps `custom` to orchestration, and `bucketOf` falls back to orchestration silently, so check membership (`lib/wall-clock-summary.js`). `dispatchesOf` turns a missing kind into `custom` (`lib/cost-read.js`): confirm a custom kind from its own row before trusting it (LIN-4426).
A full PR URL's repository and number come from `prOf` beside `prUrlsIn` (`lib/run-ledger.js`), for the task page and measure 1 alike; compare repositories case-blind, as GitHub does (LIN-4439).

A per-dispatch figure (its model, cost or completeness) is the fold's answer, carried through `lib/cost-read.js`; a reader never re-ranks `byModel` itself. `dispatchModelOf` in `lib/task-timeline.js` did, and a lane can now name two models. (Drift & Coherence Review, 13 Nov.; `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-13.md`.)

Carrying the gate's answer in the state changes the box model the renderers read. (Blind read on LIN-4439.) `ladderNotReady` asks the gate a third time, so the box and the guard order the same reasons two ways and the next close-out reason must be placed in both; one order is a decision about what the box shows versus what the guard refuses. Waiting 19 (the plan's Waiting 18): `lib/run-closeout-state.js`: the close-out reasons are bare string literals: `'blind-read-missing'` is spelled here and again in `REFUSED_REASONS` (`lib/close-out-readiness.js`, beside `'head-moved'`), and `closeOutNotReadyRefusal` builds its error by capitalising `state.message`. A reasons constant (like `CLOSE_OUT_STATUS`) covering every reason, used by the box, the guard and the render, would give them one vocabulary. (Blind read on LIN-4396.)

Waiting 20 (the plan's Waiting 19): `lib/task-timeline.js`: `dispatchModelOf` picks a dispatch's model by its own rule (`costUsd`, null as -1, then request count), while the home, `foldRequestUsage` (`lib/request-usage-fold.js`), ranks by priced dollars, then latest use, and names the latest model when nothing is priced. `modelRowOf` (`lib/cost-read.js`) drops `pricedUsd`, so the lane label (`session.model`, the fold's answer) and the rows inside it can name different models whenever any request is unpriced. The fix is for `dispatchesOf` to carry the fold's `last.model`; a change to the dominant-model rule otherwise leaves the timeline behind. (Drift & Coherence Review, 13 Nov.; `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-13.md`.)

Waiting 21 (the plan's Waiting 20): `lib/run-closeout-state.js`: `closeOutSetsDone` never asks `closeOutWaitsOn`, so the owner's check (`routes/workspace-api-run-evidence.js`) sets a stop-at-PR task Done when its landing PR is merged and approved with no blind read, while the close-out guard (`lib/close-out-readiness.js`) refuses the same trail as `blind-read-missing`, and `blindReadStep` (`lib/recommendation-blind-read.js`) then routes a read to the Done ticket (it stands aside on a completed ticket only after a close-out). The entries above name the box/guard precedence split; this is its Done path. Whether a person's own check may pass the gate is a decision; the shared-trail test runs with `byPersonCheck: false`, so it never reaches this path. (Drift & Coherence Review, 13 Nov., second read; `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-13.md`.)

fields.asked:
**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** John: "we've not been applying quite the right force to bend the curve… now want to run both real work, and some real tidies." The Drift & Coherence and Seams & Tangles reviews of 13 Nov found this area carrying rules written in two places that disagree. Batch 1 added several of them:

* Harbour can mark a task Done on a person's check before its blind read, while another check refuses that same task, and a read is then sent to a ticket that's already Done (Drift run 7, `close-out-gate-precedence-split`). John's ruling: "if I choose to do something, Harbour is a passenger. This reflects that for many real projects, they're unlikely to be exclusively changed via Harbour."
* Two pieces of code decide which PRs belong to a task, and they disagree about agent notes, so a blind read can be offered over a PR no review covered (Seams run 12, §3.0a).
* The task timeline decides which model a dispatch used by its own rule, separate from the one the cost figures use (Drift, row 150).
* The check that makes a stage wait while another is live is a runs rule, but it lives with the prompts (Seams, P-LW1).

The area's note holds 20 Waiting entries, and `lib/dispatch-store.js` is 4,530 lines. Seams also tried moving files between areas three ways, and none made the tangle smaller.

**What we want.**

* Each rule in the area has one home, and the copies are gone.
* When a person acts, Harbour follows, and that rule is written once.
* The area's Waiting entries are settled, or each says why it can't be yet.
* Each piece finishes one move and names what it retired. John: "I'd be happy to run a small variety, erring larger, to see", so piece sizes vary, leaning larger.
* The LLM & prompts side of the seam is A14's.

**Done when**

* the cases above are settled, or John has ruled they can wait;
* the area's Waiting entries are settled or say why not;
* the area reads better in a blind read after this work than before it, by more than an untouched area read at the same times.

**Every change names what it retires. Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself; only John's calls (product, money, authority, what to retire) go to him as rulings.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

fields.says: Survey @ cfd152fa4: `wakeHook.releaseNote` cannot reach most releases. The hook is built per request (`leftoverStep.forRequest`, `routes/dispatch.js:1636`, `routes/proxy-runner.js:213`) and only passed into `addFeedback`; most releases come through `_archiveItem` -> `_releaseIfHeld` (`lib/dispatch-store.js:1890`, `:1949`) from `removeItem`, `cleanup()` expiry and the stopped-run cleanup, none of which has a request or hook. Only the `_applyWakeHook` re-release (`:3429`) holds one. So put the wording on `leftoverStep` and late-bind it into the store, as `setWakeCredentialProvisionerFactory` already is (`server.js:1146`), and decide what an unbound store says (`lin-4373-leftover-step.test.js` asserts "did not run" five times). This is the second hook surface Waiting 5 (one `wakeHook`) warns about; shape it with that in mind. Do this first: it is the only part that changes the store shape, and it decides what the rewritten lin-4377 witness counts (no `formatHeldWakeNote` import in the store).

fields.asks: Plan piece 5 puts one `FEEDBACK_KINDS` table in `lib/dispatch-feedback-validation.js`. That file imports `dispatch-validation.js`, which reaches `session-telemetry.js` (via prompt-templates -> ... -> wall-clock-summary) and `dispatch-terminal.js` (via dispatch-fields -> dispatch-wake). If those import the table and build Sets from it at load, load order decides whether they hit a TDZ error. May the table live in a new import-free leaf module instead (e.g. `lib/dispatch-feedback-kinds.js`), imported by validation and the store, with the store still re-exporting `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS`?

fields.if-unanswered: Implementation builds the leaf module (an engineering call) and the PR names the departure from plan piece 5 and comments on LIN-4447.

fields.says: `findWakeEvent` has no skip rule to derive: it returns the last matching marker of any kind (`lib/dispatch-terminal.js:631`), and `lib/session-telemetry.js:82` calls it "Deliberately NOT shared". Deriving a filter would change the mint path (`lib/dispatch-store.js:3696`) and every reader of stored rows (task-page-loader, run-view, digest-feedback, run-loop-state), against the binding "never recompute pre-cutover history". Recommend: give the table a wake-role column ("every kind may carry a wake") and pin that current behaviour matches it, rather than adding a filter; the PR says this is how the done-when clause on `findWakeEvent` is met.

Prompt seam (LLM & prompts side is LIN-4448s): `lib/prompts/runner-kickoff.js` renders `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS` into the runner prompt in its current order, checked by `runner-kickoff.test.js:191`; a derived list must keep that exact order. The table also needs rows for kinds deliberately off the allowlist (`decision-answer`, `decision-withdrawal-reversed`; see `DECISION_LIFECYCLE_STAMP_KINDS`, `lib/session-telemetry.js:60`); without them a roles column quietly widens what the runner may post.

fields.what: After deriving from the kinds table, `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS` equals today's list in the same order, and the runner allowlist does not gain `decision-answer` or `decision-withdrawal-reversed`.
fields.how: A unit test pinning the exact order and membership of `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS`, alongside `runner-kickoff.test.js:191`; it fails if a row is reordered or a non-allowlist kind is admitted.

fields.says: `NEVER_RAN` has nothing to import from: `cancelled`/`expired` is spelled out at `lib/dispatch-leftover.js:29`, `lib/dispatch-store.js:1906` and `:1176`. One home must be created where neither side learns "leftover" (`lin-4377-store-knows-no-leftover`); `lib/dispatch-fields.js` is already imported by both. The other two owners are safe import-free leaves: `HALT_MODES` (`lib/workspace-halt.js`), and `followUpTarget(t) == null` (`lib/dispatch-targets.js`), equivalent to `!RESUMABLE_TARGETS.has(t || "cli")`. These are mechanical; do them last.
